endorsements.name: Cøry "interpünkt" Solovewicz
endorsements.label: You've Got Mail (That Was Meant For No One)
endorsements.description: In 2020, I registered a domain on a whim, mostly because I thought it would be hilarious for email, and then forgot about it. Then a city government faxed me their internal documents. Then an organization started sending me Cisco UCM alerts. Then 363,000 emails arrived in sixteen months. I never sent a single packet of attack traffic. The vulnerability is an assumption, that a domain nobody owns is safe to hardcode. Developers at enterprise software vendors, government agencies, and companies made that assumption. I registered the domains and the mail flowed in. This talk covers six years of passive email interception across more than 20 domains, the tooling built to systematically map this attack surface across hundreds of TLDs, and what 400,000 misdirected emails reveal about how production mail infrastructure actually fails. No exploits. No credentials. Just a $11 domain registration.
endorsements.subtitle: DEF CON 34
